newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cifra Q3 results seen lackluster.
newsitem.headline: Cifra Q3 results seen lackluster.

text.p: Third quarter results for Mexican retailer Cifra SA may be dampened by a lag in the direct impact of Mexico's economic recovery on the retail sector, analysts said.
Three analysts polled by Reuters gave an average earnings per share estimate of 0.90 peso for the quarter. Cifra's first half earnings were 636.1 million pesos.

"Because of the signs we are getting from the economy, we expect a moderate result in the third quarter of 1996, with the trend slightly improving compared to the second quarter," said Roberto Galvan of Bursametrica.
But he added that the firm will be slightly affected by low sales in areas of Mexico where Cifra has a lot of its stores -- mainly the center and south.
"The third-quarter results of Cifra will come in a little lower compared to some other retailers in the north," he said.
"If you check the figures from (retail association) ANTAD and (government statistics institute) INEGI, the areas of the center to the south are those that have lower numbers."
According to INEGI data, retail sales showed an annual negative rate of 0.7 percent in August.

Despite the lack of clear signs of a recovery in domestic consumption that would provide a boost to the compay, Cifra has been able to get by, with efficient control of operating and publicity costs and through negotiations with suppliers, keeping financial margins and sales stable.
"The company in general terms looks good; they stopped their expansion plans a little, but I think it was a good strategy while they consolidated," said Rolando Calderon of brokerage Santander.
The biggest falls in retail sales were in the central and southern cities of Oaxaca, Cuernavaca, Mexico City, Tuxtla Gutierrez, Mrida and Toluca, among others, INEGI said.
ANTAD said in its August report that the southeast and Mexico City areas showed the biggest falls in sales, with drops of 10.2 percent and 8.6 percent respectively.
Caldern projected sales in the third quarter of 5.6 billion pesos, operating profit of 225 million pesos, an integral financing gain of 186 million pesos and net profits of 293 million pesos.

Analysts agreed that the fourth quarter will be better for Cifra and other retailers as domestic consumption gradually picks up. "The fourth quarter will be good because then these companies report the extraordinary profit from their pension funds, obviously it is stronger for seasonal reasons," said Esteban Galndez of Caspian Research.

"I think it is a good time to accumulate paper such as that of Cifra or (fellow retailer) Soriana because they will give us a growing last quarter after being very punished before," said a Monterrey-based analyst who declined to be named.
